standard_prerequisites.name: No rational tails or bridges under ampleness
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components; Same chapter, Lemmas lemma-rational-tail-negative and lemma-rational-bridge-zero
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows X contains no rational tails or bridges, which also rules out degree-zero restrictions of omega_X to reduced connected subschemes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Global generation of the tricanonical sheaf
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that omega_X^tensor 3 is globally generated once tails and bridges are absent.

standard_prerequisites.name: Separation criterion and descent to the algebraic closure
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces closed immerseness to surjectivity of H^0(X, L) -> H^0(Z, L|_Z) for every degree-2 subscheme Z, and lets one replace k by its algebraic closure.

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing on Gorenstein curves and the tail inequality
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemmas lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein and lemma-no-rational-tail; Duality for Schemes, Section duality-section-dualizing (Gorenstein hypothesis)
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the surjectivity problem into the inequality 3 deg(omega_X|_Y) > -2 chi(Y, O_Y) + deg(Z cap Y) and supplies the bound away from the exceptional cases.

core_obligations: Tails and bridges are absent by the ampleness input, so omega_X^tensor 3 is globally generated; after extending k to its algebraic closure one must check surjectivity onto every degree-2 closed subscheme Z, i.e. H^1(X, I L) = 0.

By the Gorenstein vanishing lemma it suffices to prove 3 deg(omega_X|_Y) > -2 chi(Y, O_Y) + deg(Z cap Y) for every reduced connected closed subscheme Y, which becomes 3 deg(omega_X|_Y) > -2 + 2 dim H^1(Y, O_Y) + deg(Z cap Y) since H^0(Y, O_Y) = k.

The inequality holds by lemma-no-rational-tail except when Y = X or deg(omega_X|_Y) = 0; the latter is impossible because omega_X is ample (first lemma cited), and for Y = X Riemann-Roch with g >= 2 gives the bound.
The same argument with Z empty gives H^1(X, omega_X^tensor 3) = 0.
proof_roadmap: Derive absence of tails and bridges from ampleness of omega_X and conclude omega_X^tensor 3 is globally generated.
Descend to k algebraically closed and reformulate very ampleness as surjectivity onto every degree-2 subscheme.
Use the Gorenstein vanishing criterion to reduce to a degree inequality on reduced connected subschemes.
Handle the two exceptional cases of the inequality: degree-zero restrictions (excluded by ampleness) and Y = X (Riemann-Roch, g >= 2).
Conclude the closed immersion and, with Z empty, the vanishing of H^1.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the tricanonical very-ampleness statement for nodal curves of genus at least 2 with ample dualizing sheaf (statement lines 6791-6795). The proof (lines 6797-6852) chains: absence of tails and bridges, global generation of omega^3, descent to the algebraic closure, the degree-2 subscheme separation criterion, the Gorenstein vanishing reduction, a degree inequality from lemma-no-rational-tail with two exceptional cases closed by ampleness and by Riemann-Roch. Every step is present with no omitted details. H3: a multi-ingredient research-level chain orchestrating four prior results around a quantitative inequality.
